checks.what: Removing the 1431 HRE loss of 25 cells to electorate-of-trier is supported. The page puts the electorate 'along the river Moselle between Trier, near the French border, and Koblenz on the Rhine' and dates no gain in 1430-1440 (only the electors Raban von Helmstatt and Jakob I von Sierck). Keyframe holy-roman-empire-minor-states_1431b (adjust, 1431-1647) resolves to the 25 cells. The HRE Cliopatria shape holds 0 of them in 1431-1555, 1 in 1556-1641 and all 25 from 1648, and the Trier dossier's corrected Moselle shapes share none of them, so the change keeps them in the Empire and adds no break at 1431 or 1648. The electorate-of-trier change is a notes line only, and it is accurate. Errors found and corrected: (1) the cells are not the Hunsrueck-Nahe country. Their centroids lie at 7.1-8.7 E, 49.0-49.8 N: the Palatinate (Westrich, Palatinate Forest, the Rhine plain about Speyer, Heidelberg and Wissembourg). (2) The note said the event left all 25 cells ownerless, but the electoral-palatinate dossier draws 20 of them (Speyer and Worms overlap those), so the size rule gives those 20 to it. Only 5 would have had no owner: the cells about Zweibruecken, Kusel, St. Wendel and Wissembourg. (3) The note cited keyframes 1642 and 1645 as already treating Spanish-held land as Imperial, but neither correction reaches these cells; Cliopatria gives 24 of them to kingdom-of-spain in 1642-1647. I rewrote the 1431b correction.text and note to match (land label, the 20 cells drawn by electoral-palatinate and the 5 unowned ones, keyframe 1632 only, and that this keyframe keeps the Spanish-held years as Imperial land under occupation). Re-validated with --resolve: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Residual risk, not fixed: for 1642-1647 the keyframe gives about 5 cells to the Empire against Cliopatria's Spanish hold, on no page.
